## Internment letter to Mackensen's soldiers' council — p226 C / p227 A

**Sources on this page:** p227 A4. [Concise case study](../military/mackensen_internment.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p226 C1](226.md#source-p226-c1), [p226 C2](226.md#source-p226-c2), [p226 C3](226.md#source-p226-c3).

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-internment-internment-letter-to-mackensens-soldiers-council--p226-c--p227-a"></a>



**Prior reading: J. Rives Childs; George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Source edition and exact repair audit: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The four-part letter says that efforts to avoid internment have failed, asks the soldiers to maintain order, and expresses the hope of their return to Germany. This body is already published in [Lasry et al., Table 4](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf), printed p. 22, and in [Lasry's dissertation, Table 6.4](https://www.uni-kassel.de/upress/online/OpenAccess/978-3-7376-0458-1.OpenAccess.pdf), p. 108. The source edition explains a two-location defect in part 3. An independent Berlin copy now supports the signature repairs and exposes differences between the transmitted and archival wording.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-internment-meaning"></a>

### Meaning

Addressed to the soldiers' council of the Mackensen army, the letter reports that the Entente insists on internment. It says that maintaining the marching order would be treated as a breach of the armistice, giving the Entente grounds to enter Germany. The sender promises to seek tolerable internment conditions and a safe return home after peace is concluded, then urges calm and order to avoid internal disintegration.

The closing names the executive council of the workers' and soldiers' councils of Greater Berlin. The raw signatures are `SOLKENBUHR` and `MNELLER`. The archival counterpart signs Molkenbuhr and Richard Müller, supporting the two surname repairs described below.

The source is headed `ZON v BSL` (the O has two marks), `04.20 a.m., December 2nd`, with origin field `NR 132 2200 (11/29) 4 TLE`. Parts 1–3 appear on printed p226 and part 4 on p227. These are different date fields, not an interchangeable date of composition. All four parts use the unchanged published **Nov28–Dec1** key.

| Part | Printed coordinates | Fixed raw positions, including garbles | Additional readable-text repairs |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p226 C1 | 344 | 172/172 | 6 substitutions with the damaged word retained; 8 if `STATIONEN` is proposed |
| p226 C2 | 324 | 162/162 | 11 known-coordinate substitutions |
| p226 C3 | 338 | 168/169 under the explicit group-restoration model | 4 substitutions and 1 supplied coordinate |
| p227 A4 | 392 | 196/196 | 12 substitutions; 13 if `MOLKENBUHR` is also proposed |

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-internment-an-independent-berlin-copy"></a>

### An independent Berlin copy

Document 96 in Engel, Holtz and Materna, eds., *Groß-Berliner Arbeiter- und
Soldatenräte in der Revolution 1918/19* (Akademie Verlag, 1993), pp. 461–462,
preserves a typescript carbon copy of the same letter. Its 28 November
dateline and the editor's 29 November dispatch date distinguish composition
from transmission; Childs records `2200 (11/29)` in the originating line.
[Published source and comparison](../../experiments/mackensen_archival_comparison/README.md).

The independent signatures support the existing cipher-side proposals:

| Raw surname | Signature in the Berlin copy | Required source-coordinate change |
|---|---|---|
| `SOLKENBUHR` | Molkenbuhr | 71: V→F |
| `MNELLER` | Richard Müller | 269: G→D |

Indices are zero based. Each surname needs one substitution. The complete
fourth-part edition with both names still costs **13 substitutions**; the
new evidence strengthens those earlier repairs. Richard belongs to the
archival attribution, while the ciphertext supplies only the surname.

The copy also has *Faktoren* where the received first part yields
`SMUTIONEN`, and a longer armistice term in part 2. These are distinct
textual witnesses. The comparison uses the published transcription;
the archival original has not been inspected.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-internment-part-3-restoring-two-malformed-groups"></a>

### Part 3: restoring two malformed groups

The source visibly prints a six-letter group **`VFFGDV`** at group 34 and a four-letter group **`XFVA`** at group 56. The total remains the advertised 338 coordinates. Decrypting those coordinates in their printed sequence gives a garbled result; that identity result is retained in the certificate.

A separate model restores five-letter grouping at those two locations: remove one coordinate from group 34 and add one slot inside group 56. Among all **30** local layouts, the readable 169-position candidate needs the fewest further known-coordinate substitutions in two equivalent cases:

- Remove either of the adjacent `F` characters in group 34, producing `VFGDV`.
- Supply `V` after the initial `X` of group 56, producing `XVFVA`.

The two deletion indices are aliases of one reconstructed stream. Before supplying the new coordinate or changing any remaining source symbol, its raw plaintext is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion-and-insertion frame; equivalent deletion aliases retained:**

```text
ESIVTUNSE?BEMUEHENEUREINTERNIERUNGSOZUGESTALTENDASSIHRWEDERNHTNOCHMANGELLEIDETUNDNACHDEMMOJGLICHSTRASCHENFRIEDENSCHLUSSGLUECKLICHUNDGESUNDINDIEHEIMATZUJUECKKEHRENKOENNTY
```

</details>

Four explicit coordinate substitutions and the one supplied `V` give:

**Readable German — conditional reconstructed third part:**

> Es ist unser Bemühen, eure Internierung so zu gestalten, dass ihr weder Not noch Mangel leidet und nach dem möglichst raschen Friedenschluss glücklich und gesund in die Heimat zurückkehren könnt.

The source-length spelling `FRIEDENSCHLUSS` is retained in the exact candidate; the additional S of modern `FRIEDENSSCHLUSS` is not silently inserted. The local optimum is conditional on this candidate and the stated two-group model. It establishes a small exact repair certificate, not historical certainty about every error.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-internment-a-word-in-part-1-remains-unsettled"></a>

### A word in part 1 remains unsettled

The directly decrypted token after `INBEDRACHTKOQMENDEN` is **`SMUTIONEN`**, occupying nine positions. The prior publication prints **`SITUATIONEN`**, which has eleven. That normalization therefore requires two extra plaintext positions and is not an unchanged or same-length decryption.

The present certificate prices two same-length alternatives. `STATIONEN` adds two coordinate substitutions to the six otherwise proposed in part 1; `INSTANZEN` raises that total to seventeen. The archival counterpart has `FAKTOREN`, eight letters. That wording explains the reference to the bodies concerned but does not fit the nine received positions. The conservative cipher edition therefore retains `SMUTIONEN`; `STATIONEN` remains a separately priced alternative, and the earlier `SITUATIONEN` normalization remains attributed to its publication.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-internment-literal-source-and-reproducibility"></a>

## Late-November cipher and routing instructions — p225–228

**Sources on this page:** p227 B. [Concise case study](../radio/late_november_cipher_instructions.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p225 A](225.md#source-p225-a), [p226 B2](226.md#source-p226-b2), [p228 C1](228.md#source-p228-c1), [p228 C2](228.md#source-p228-c2).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-late-november-cipher-and-routing-instructions--p225228"></a>



**Source reading and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Published period keys: George Lasry and collaborators.**

Five ciphertext records and one cleartext notice describe missing December key tables, proposed sharing of keys, a fragment of a numerical-code instruction, and direct routing to an army station. All ciphertext below is read with the unchanged published **Nov28–Dec1** key. These messages give evidence about specific communications arrangements; they do not assign a key to an unresolved challenge.

| Record | Received slots | Fixed raw positions, including garbles | Content |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p225 A | 232 | 110/116; completed 116/116 | UKS to use a November key from 1 December because December tables have not arrived |
| p226 B2 | 208 | 104/104 | Surviving continuation about reading numerical sequences backwards |
| p227 B | 152 | 76/76 | Send messages for the army and subordinate formations directly to ZOEN |
| p228 C1 | 176 | 88/88 | Agreement involving UKS, ZOEN and BSL about the December key |
| p228 C2 | 144 | 72/72 | BSL and UKS should use the same key; UKS agrees |
| p227 C | Cleartext | Not a decipherment | ITOCHI parts cannot be deciphered; request RICHI or plaintext |

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-november-key-reused-because-december-tables-are-missing"></a>

### November key reused because December tables are missing

**Readable German — six compatible fills and two word repairs:**

> Station UKS chiffr. ab ersten Dez. mit NSL Nov., da Dez.-Tafeln noch nicht
> eingegangen. Bitte Telegr. an uns ebenfalls mit NSL Nov. schluesseln.

UKS reports that December tables have not arrived and requests reciprocal
use of the material labelled `NSL NOV` from 1 December. The two occurrences
of `NSL` are retained. The abbreviation does not identify a particular
November day's key.

The notice is headed `BSL v UKS (09.24 p.m., November 28th)`,
`2200 (28/11)`, `RIZI-232`. Its native frame has **232 slots**, including
five printed dashes and the invalid `R` in `DFGVR`. Six compatible word fills
complete **116/116 positions** while retaining all **226 valid coordinates**.
Reading `NICGT` as `NICHT` and `TELEGD` as `TELEGR` costs two additional
observed-coordinate substitutions. The quotation uses that edited layer,
with editorial spacing and punctuation.

```

**Edited output — six source-mask fills; zero observed-coordinate substitutions:**

STATIONUKSCHIFFRABERSTENDEZMITNSLNOVYDADEZTAFELNNOCHNICGTEINGEGANGENYBITTETELEGDANUNSEBENFALLSMITNSLNOVSCHLUESSELNYY
```

**Edited output — the same six fills and two observed-coordinate substitutions:**

| Observed coordinates changed | 6: A→D; 9: F→V |

Indices are zero based. Each completed letter retains one observed half-pair.
The unenciphered annotation after the body remains separate.

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-an-explicit-agreement-to-use-the-same-key"></a>

### An explicit agreement to use the same key

p228 C is headed `BSL v ZON` (the O has two marks), `04.47 a.m., December 1st`, `0420 (11/30) 2 TLE`. Both parts are directly readable without any coordinate repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — two separate source parts under the unchanged key:**

```text
p228 C1
MITYUKSYVEREINBARTEYZOENYDEZEMBERSCHLUESSELWIEYBSLYZWISCHENYBSLYUNDYZOENYVORGESCHLAGENYY

p228 C2
IMVERKEHRYBSLYUNDYUKSYGLEICHENSCHLUESSELVERWENDENYYUKSYISTEINVERSTANDENY
```

</details>

The first part reports an arrangement with UKS concerning the December key as proposed between BSL and ZOEN. The second is explicit: use the same key in BSL–UKS traffic, and UKS agrees. Together, the two source streams retain **320/320 coordinates** and directly fix **160/160 plaintext positions**. This does not establish which particular November day's key the parties subsequently used. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p228_C.png).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-numerical-code-fragment-and-army-routing"></a>

### Numerical-code fragment and army routing

p226 B2 says that its first part is missing. The surviving continuation directly gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ZAHLENREIHENVONRUECKWAERTSGELESENYSODASSXYXSZ8HLEN3Y5Y9YX5YX0YUYSYWYYBENUTZENSIEGLEICHESMITUNFYANTWORTYY
```

</details>

The beginning says that numerical sequences are read backwards; the end asks the recipient to use the same procedure in communication with the sender and to answer. `Z8HLEN → ZAHLEN` and `MITUNF → MITUNS` cost two coordinate substitutions. The central examples, including `XYXS` and `3Y5Y9YX5YX0`, remain literal. The missing first part and those garbles prevent reconstruction of a complete numerical-code rule. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p226_B2.png).

p227 B directly reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BITTEFUNKSPRUECHEANXXYARMEEUNDUNTERSTEL6TEFORMATIONENUNMITTELBARANZOENGEBENY
```

</details>

Restoring `UNTERSTELLTE` costs one coordinate substitution. The raw army field **`XX`** is retained, without silently treating it as an Arabic number or Roman numeral. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p227_B.png).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-separate-historical-interpretation-of-the-army-field"></a>

### Separate historical interpretation of the army field

The later [unit-based key-label review](../../experiments/late_key_interpretation/README.md) applies the optional p230 map to p227 B. Baseline `X→1` and the separate `Y→X` separator convention give **11th Army**; with the already counted one-coordinate repair of `UNTERSTELLTE`, the instruction asks for telegrams to the 11th Army and subordinate formations to be sent directly to ZOEN. The baseline text above remains the unchanged-key result. Applying the same declared layers to p226 B2 leaves its numerical examples damaged and does not recover the missing code rule.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-a-cleartext-request-to-avoid-an-unreadable-cipher"></a>

### A cleartext request to avoid an unreadable cipher

p227 C, headed `BSL v UKS`, `2316 (11/28) K. M. BERLIN`, says that parts 3 and 4 of a referenced War Department message in **ITOCHI** cannot be deciphered. It requests **RICHI or plaintext**, then asks that ciphering be avoided if possible in future. This is a directly visible unencrypted source notice, not a new cryptanalytic result. The literal misspellings and the trailing forwarding annotation are retained in the input record. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p227_C.png).

## An instruction to avoid fighting, with further orders to follow

**Sources on this page:** p227 D. [Concise case study](../military/avoid_fighting_instruction.md).

<a id="edition-cases-military-avoid-fighting-instruction-an-instruction-to-avoid-fighting-with-further-orders-to-follow"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

An instruction to OKM requires avoidance of all fighting, compliance with demands abbreviated FRANZ, and attention to further orders. A joint reading with p225 recovers JEDER from its original coordinate pair. Only the word repair ZT to ZU remains, reducing the cost from four observed-coordinate substitutions to two.

<a id="edition-cases-military-avoid-fighting-instruction-source-and-scope"></a>

### Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p227 excerpt](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/sources/p227_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/certificates.json)

The published `Nov28-Dec1` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p227 D](#edition-cases-military-avoid-fighting-instruction-p227-d) | 272 | 136 / 136 | 4; **2 with shared J** | 0 |

<a id="edition-cases-military-avoid-fighting-instruction-p227-d"></a>

### p227 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) UKS v BSL (09.29 a.m., November 28th); KR 0912 (11/28); RICHI-272`

**Conditional interpretation — shared FA=J, with the two-coordinate ZT to ZU repair:**

> OKM. Auf Befehl der REICHSLEITG ist jeder Kampf zu vermeiden. Eingehen
> auf FRANZ Forderungen notwendig. Weitere Befehle folgen.
> OHL1A1136?GEH. OP2ANG.

The J at plaintext position 31 comes from the complete observed pair `FA`
at source positions 3 and 105. [p225 B2](../military/regimental_journey_report.md#p225-b2)
provides a second native instance in `JEDE UNTERSTUETZUNG`.
The shared letter interpretation fixes **135/136 positions** in this message,
leaving the reference `1136?`; `FRANZ` remains abbreviated.
It extends the existing Nov28–Dec1 interpretation, including its historical
numeral assumptions. [Joint evidence and 24 square witnesses](../../experiments/late_november_joint_completion/README.md).

The subsequent [calendar and unit comparison](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
also fixes the original `VG` pair in the reference as `7`:

| Field | After the shared J | After the unit interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| OHL reference | `1136?` | **11367** |

The conditional reading now fixes **136/136 positions**. Its two-coordinate
`ZT→ZU` repair is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
OKMYAUFBEFEHLDERREICHSLEITGYIST1EDERKAMPFZTVERMEIDENYEINGEHENAUFFRANZYFORDERUNGENNOTWENDIGYWEITEREBEFEHLEFOLGENYYOHLXAXX280GEHYOPJANGYYY
```

**Edited output — earlier unchanged-key wording; 4 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
OKMYAUFBEFEHLDERREICHSLEITGYISTJEDERKAMPFZUVERMEIDENYEINGEHENAUFFRANZYFORDERUNGENNOTWENDIGYWEITEREBEFEHLEFOLGENYYOHLXAXX280GEHYOPJANGYYY
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> OKM. Auf Befehl der REICHSLEITG ist jeder Kampf zu vermeiden. Eingehen auf FRANZ Forderungen notwendig. Weitere Befehle folgen. OHLXAXX280GEH. OPJANG.

**Meaning:** The message instructs OKM, on the order of the authority labeled REICHSLEITG, to avoid any fighting, says compliance with demands labeled FRANZ is necessary, and promises further orders. FRANZ is read as an abbreviation for French in this context; the source does not spell that word out. The message records an instruction, not proof that fighting stopped or that the demands were fulfilled.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 272 printed coordinates are present and legible, with no source erasures. The source photograph includes a complete group absent from the earlier OCR; restoring that visible group is a transcription correction, not an inserted historical coordinate.
- The high-resolution source reads FFFVD, including the third F with its middle bar. It is not treated as an invented missing coordinate or a T-shaped source mask.
- Under the published square, 1EDER to JEDER and ZT to ZU cost four substitutions. The shared FA=J interpretation removes the two J repairs; ZT to ZU still costs two. REICHSLEITG and FRANZ remain abbreviated.
- Y is the separator in this period key. The closing OHLXAXX280GEH and OPJANG are preserved literally; 280 is not turned into a calendar date or a reference number with an inferred format.

<a id="edition-cases-military-avoid-fighting-instruction-evidence-credit-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce the source edition with `python experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/verify.py --verify` and the joint extension with `python experiments/late_november_joint_completion/verify.py --verify`. The source verifier accepts `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` for the original PDF and exact crop pixels.
